rubric.why: Atomic number is the key basis used to arrange the elements in the modern periodic table.
rubric.description: Identifies atomic number as the basis of the arrangement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark if the answer identifies atomic number as the basis for arranging elements.

rubric.why: The defining arrangement is in order of increasing atomic number.
rubric.description: States that elements are arranged in increasing atomic number.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the elements are arranged according to increasing atomic number.

modelAnswer: The modern periodic table is based upon the arrangement of elements according to increasing atomic number.

rubric.why: Periodicity refers to properties recurring at regular intervals.
rubric.description: States that properties of elements repeat at regular intervals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the repetition of element properties after regular intervals.

rubric.why: The name for this repeating trend in properties is periodicity.
rubric.description: Names the trend as periodicity in the properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the trend as periodicity in the properties.

modelAnswer: As a whole the periodic table shows the repetition of the properties of elements after regular intervals. This trend is called periodicity in the properties.

rubric.why: A period corresponds to completing a shell, whose electron capacity is fixed.
rubric.description: States that each period represents shell completion and/or that a shell has a fixed electron capacity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking a period to shell completion or the fixed number of electrons accommodated in a shell.

rubric.why: The fixed shell capacities lead to fixed numbers of elements in successive periods, which increase in the listed sequence.
rubric.description: States that the number of elements in periods is fixed by shell capacity, or gives the successive period counts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the number of elements per period is fixed by shell capacity or giving the sequence 2, 8, 8, 18, 18, 32 and 32.

modelAnswer: Each period also represents the completion of a shell. Since the number of electrons to be accommodated in a particular shell is fixed, the number of elements in a period is also fixed. The number of elements in successive periods is 2, 8, 8, 18, 18, 32 and 32.

rubric.why: Members of a group have the same number of electrons in their outermost shells.
rubric.description: States that group members have the same number of outermost-shell electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the shared number of electrons in the outermost shell.

rubric.why: The textbook answer links the shared outermost electrons with similar chemical properties.
rubric.description: States that elements in a group resemble one another in chemical properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that elements in a group have similar or resembling chemical properties.

modelAnswer: Elements present in a group resemble one another in their chemical properties since they contain the same number of electrons in their outermost shells.

rubric.why: The answer must give the correct comparison: sodium is more reactive than calcium.
rubric.description: Correctly states that calcium is not more reactive; sodium is more reactive than calcium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for answering no and identifying sodium as more reactive than calcium.

rubric.why: Sodium loses its single outermost electron more easily; metal reactivity depends on the tendency to lose electrons.
rubric.description: Explains the comparison using electron loss, including sodium's one outermost electron and calcium's two, or the tendency of metals to lose electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the reactivity in terms of easier electron loss or the tendency of metals to lose electrons.

modelAnswer: No. Sodium is more reactive than calcium because sodium has one electron in its outermost shell and loses it more easily, while calcium has two outermost electrons. The chemical reactivity of metals depends on their tendency to lose electrons.

rubric.why: The first electron is easier to remove from a neutral magnesium atom.
rubric.description: States that magnesium's first electron is easier to remove.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that the first electron is easier to remove.

rubric.why: After the first electron is removed, removing the second is more difficult, so the second ionization energy is greater.
rubric.description: Contrasts removal of the first and second electrons, or states that the second ionization energy is greater.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that removing the second electron is harder than removing the first.

modelAnswer: It is easier to remove the first electron from magnesium than the second one.
